# package client

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-openadr/client"
```

Package client holds the two clients of a VTN: VEN, for a virtual end node, and BL, for the Business Logic of a utility or aggregator. Both speak OpenADR 3.1.0 over HTTP, or 3.0.1 with Config.Version, and differ only in the operations they offer, which follow the scopes the specification gives each role.

A client is safe for concurrent use. Its methods take a context that bounds the whole call, including a token request it may have to make first.

Failures reported by the VTN are returned as \*openadr.Error and match the sentinels of package openadr, such as openadr.ErrNotFound, with errors.Is. An object that does not satisfy the schema is rejected before any request is sent, with an \*openadr.ValidationError.

## Functions

### func Each

```go
func Each[T any](ctx context.Context, search func(context.Context, Page) ([]T, error)) iter.Seq2[T, error]
```

Each iterates over a whole search result, fetching it page by page with search. It stops at the first error, which it yields with a zero value.

	for event, err := range client.Each(ctx, func(ctx context.Context, p client.Page) ([]openadr.Event, error) {
		return ven.Events(ctx, client.EventQuery{ProgramID: id, Page: p})
	}) {
		...
	}

The result is not a snapshot: objects created or deleted while iterating may be skipped or seen twice.

A full page that is the same as the one before it means a VTN that does not honour skip: Each then yields an error that matches openadr.ErrProtocol instead of asking for the same page for ever. A VTN that keeps returning full pages of new objects is not told from a long result: bound it with ctx.

### type AttemptMetrics

```go
type AttemptMetrics interface {
	// OnAttempt is called after each attempt. attempt counts from 1; err
	// is nil for the attempt that succeeded. A call that is not retried
	// has one attempt.
	OnAttempt(op string, attempt int, duration time.Duration, err error)
}
```

AttemptMetrics is an optional extension of Metrics: when the value given as Config.Metrics also implements it, it is told of every attempt of a call, which is where retries show.

### type Config

```go
type Config struct {
	// BaseURL is the URL of the VTN's API, the one the paths of the
	// specification, such as /programs, are appended to. Required.
	BaseURL string
	// Version is the revision of OpenADR the VTN speaks: openadr.Version310
	// (the default when empty) or openadr.Version301. See
	// openadr.Version301 for what a 3.0.1 client does differently.
	Version openadr.Version
	// HTTPClient makes the requests; it is where TLS, proxies and timeouts
	// are configured. When nil, a client with a 30 second timeout is used.
	// A client without a CheckRedirect of its own follows a redirect only
	// to the scheme, host and port the request went to: elsewhere the
	// bearer token, or the client secret of a token request, would follow
	// it. A redirect it does not follow is answered as the status it is.
	HTTPClient *http.Client
	// Credentials authenticate with the OAuth2 client-credentials flow.
	Credentials *Credentials
	// Tokens supplies bearer tokens some other way. Set at most one of
	// Credentials and Tokens; with neither, requests carry no token, which
	// only a VTN that does not authenticate will accept.
	Tokens TokenSource
	// UserAgent is sent with every request when not empty.
	UserAgent string
	// MaxResponseBytes limits the size of a response body; 16 MiB when zero.
	MaxResponseBytes int64
	// RetryPolicy decides whether a call that failed in a way another
	// attempt can cure is tried again, and after how long: see
	// RetryPolicy for which failures those are. When nil, nothing is
	// retried (NoRetry); ExponentialBackoff is the usual choice.
	RetryPolicy RetryPolicy
	// RetryCreates lets the policy also retry a create whose fate is not
	// known: the connection was lost, or a gateway got no answer. The VTN
	// may then have created the object, and the second attempt may create
	// it again, or be answered with openadr.ErrConflict where names are
	// unique. Without it such a create is returned to the caller, who can
	// look before trying again.
	RetryCreates bool
	// Metrics receives a callback for every call; see Metrics. Nil
	// disables them.
	Metrics Metrics
	// Logger receives what a client does beside what it returns: at debug
	// level every call, with its operation, duration and outcome; at info
	// level a token that was renewed because the VTN refused the old one;
	// at warn level every retry. Never bodies, tokens or secrets. Nil
	// disables logging.
	Logger *slog.Logger
}
```

Config configures a client.

### type ExponentialBackoffConfig

```go
type ExponentialBackoffConfig struct {
	// BaseDelay is the wait before the second attempt, doubled before
	// each one after; 200 ms when zero.
	BaseDelay time.Duration
	// MaxDelay is the longest wait; 30 seconds when zero.
	MaxDelay time.Duration
	// MaxAttempts is how many attempts a call gets, the first included; 4
	// when zero. A negative number is no limit: then give every call a
	// context with a deadline.
	MaxAttempts int
	// RetryOnTimeout also retries a call that timed out. Off by default: a
	// call that used up its time once will often do so again, and a
	// caller that set a short timeout meant it.
	RetryOnTimeout bool
	// NoJitter turns off the randomizing of the wait. By default each
	// wait is somewhere between half of and the whole computed delay, so
	// that clients that failed together do not come back together.
	NoJitter bool
}
```

ExponentialBackoffConfig configures NewExponentialBackoff.

### type Metrics

```go
type Metrics interface {
	// OnRequest is called when a call begins.
	OnRequest(op string)
	// OnResponse is called when a call succeeded.
	OnResponse(op string, duration time.Duration)
	// OnError is called when a call failed for any reason but time. err is
	// what the method returns: test it with errors.Is and errors.As.
	OnError(op string, duration time.Duration, err error)
	// OnTimeout is called when a call ran out of time: the error matches
	// openadr.ErrTimeout.
	OnTimeout(op string, duration time.Duration)
}
```

Metrics receives a callback for every call a client makes to a VTN. A call is what a method of VEN or BL does, however many HTTP requests that takes: a token request before it and retries are part of the call.

op names the operation as the specification does, by method and path, with {id} in the place of an ID: "GET /events", "PUT /programs/{id}", "GET /notifiers/mqtt/topics/vens/{id}/events". The set of values is small and fixed, so it is fit to be a label.

The callbacks run on the goroutine of the call and must not block: count, observe, return. Implementations must be safe for concurrent use.

Every call gives one OnRequest and then exactly one of the other three.

### type NotificationStream

```go
type NotificationStream struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

NotificationStream is an open WebSocket with a VTN, on which the VTN sends the notifications of the client's subscriptions that name openadr.MechanismWebSocket.

WebSocket notifications are not part of OpenADR 3.1.0; a VTN says in GET /notifiers whether it has them. Package notification/websocket keeps a stream open across failures, which is what a program usually wants.

#### func (NotificationStream) Close

```go
func (s *NotificationStream) Close() error
```

Close ends the stream. A Next that is waiting returns an error. Close may be called from any goroutine, and more than once.

#### func (NotificationStream) KeepAlive

```go
func (s *NotificationStream) KeepAlive(interval time.Duration)
```

KeepAlive makes the stream ping the VTN every interval, and makes Next fail when nothing at all was heard from the VTN for two and a half intervals: a connection that died without a word is noticed that way. Call it before the first Next.

#### func (NotificationStream) Next

```go
func (s *NotificationStream) Next() (openadr.Notification, error)
```

Next waits for the next notification. An error ends the stream: Close it and open another. One goroutine at a time may call Next.

### type RetryPolicy

```go
type RetryPolicy interface {
	// ShouldRetry is called after a failed attempt that can be retried.
	// attempt counts the attempts made so far, from 1. It returns whether
	// to try again and how long to wait first. When the VTN named a wait
	// in a Retry-After header and it is longer, the client waits that long.
	// A wait that would outlast the deadline of the call's context is not
	// begun: the call fails at once, with the error of the last attempt.
	ShouldRetry(attempt int, err error) (retry bool, wait time.Duration)
}
```

RetryPolicy decides whether a failed call is tried again, and after how long. It is consulted only for failures that can be retried at all, which the client decides and a policy cannot widen:

  - the failure is one that another attempt can cure: no answer (a connection that could not be made or was lost, a timeout), or an answer that says to come back: 429, 502, 503 or 504;
  - repeating the request cannot do twice what was asked once. A read, an update and a delete can always be repeated. A create (POST) is repeated only when it certainly did not reach the VTN (the connection could not be made, or the answer was 429 or 503), unless Config.RetryCreates says otherwise.

A cancelled context, a 4xx other than 429, a 500 and an invalid object are never retried. Neither is the one retry with a fresh token after a 401 a matter for the policy: that always happens, once.

Implementations must be safe for concurrent use.

#### func ExponentialBackoff

```go
func ExponentialBackoff(base, maxDelay time.Duration, maxAttempts int) RetryPolicy
```

ExponentialBackoff returns a policy that waits base before the second attempt and twice as long before each one after, up to maxDelay, and gives up after maxAttempts attempts. It is NewExponentialBackoff with the rest left at its defaults.

#### func NewExponentialBackoff

```go
func NewExponentialBackoff(cfg ExponentialBackoffConfig) RetryPolicy
```

NewExponentialBackoff returns a policy of exponential backoff.

#### func NoRetry

```go
func NoRetry() RetryPolicy
```

NoRetry returns the policy that never retries, which is the default.

### type TokenSource

```go
type TokenSource interface {
	Token(ctx context.Context) (string, error)
}
```

TokenSource supplies the bearer token for a request. Implementations must be safe for concurrent use.

A TokenSource that also has a method Invalidate(token string) is told when the VTN rejects a token with 401; the request is then retried once with the next token it returns.

### type VEN

```go
type VEN struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

VEN is the client of a virtual end node. It reads programs and events, reports on them, and maintains the VEN's own ven and resource objects.

A VTN shows a VEN only the reports, vens and resources created with its own credentials; asking for another client's object fails with openadr.ErrNotFound.

```go
func (c *VEN) MQTTTopics(ctx context.Context, of TopicSet) (openadr.Topics, error)
```

MQTTTopics asks the VTN on which MQTT topics it publishes the operations on a set of objects. Subscribe to them with package notification/mqtt.

#### func (VEN) NotificationStream

```go
func (c *VEN) NotificationStream(ctx context.Context) (*NotificationStream, error)
```

NotificationStream opens a WebSocket on which the VTN sends the notifications of this client's subscriptions that name openadr.MechanismWebSocket. ctx bounds opening it, not its life. A VTN without WebSockets answers with openadr.ErrNotFound.

#### func (VEN) Notifiers

```go
func (c *VEN) Notifiers(ctx context.Context) (openadr.Notifiers, error)
```

Notifiers asks the VTN how it notifies: by webhook, by MQTT, or both.

#### func (VEN) Resource

```go
func (c *VEN) Resource(ctx context.Context, id string) (openadr.Resource, error)
```

Resource returns the resource with the given ID. OpenADR 3.0.1 reaches a resource through its VEN: use ResourceOf.

#### func (VEN) ResourceGroup

```go
func (c *VEN) ResourceGroup(ctx context.Context, id string) (openadr.ResourceGroup, error)
```

ResourceGroup returns the resource group with the given ID.

#### func (VEN) ResourceGroups

```go
func (c *VEN) ResourceGroups(ctx context.Context, q ResourceGroupQuery) ([]openadr.ResourceGroup, error)
```

ResourceGroups searches the resource groups that hold a resource of this VEN, directly or through other groups. Of their children the VTN shows those resources and such groups only.

#### func (VEN) ResourceOf

```go
func (c *VEN) ResourceOf(ctx context.Context, venID, id string) (openadr.Resource, error)
```

ResourceOf returns the resource with the given ID of the VEN with the given ID. It works with both revisions; in 3.1.0, where a resource is reached by its ID alone, venID is not sent.

```go
func (c *VEN) Resources(ctx context.Context, q ResourceQuery) ([]openadr.Resource, error)
```

Resources searches the resources of this VEN.

UpdateResource replaces the resource that has res.ID with res. Targets are not sent and keep the value Business Logic gave them.


UpdateVEN replaces the VEN that has v.ID with v. Targets are not sent and keep the value Business Logic gave them.


### type VENQuery

```go
type VENQuery struct {
	Name string
	// Targets and TargetType work as in ProgramQuery.
	Targets    []string
	TargetType string
	Page
}
```

VENQuery filters a search for VENs.
